supporting_observations.claim: At 13:45:45 UTC, PowerShell ran on WS-JFROST-01 as ali.hassan with the exact command used in the documented workstation-patching practice: it ran \\FILE-MAP-01\IT\Patch-Workstations.ps1. The following wusa.exe process installed a Windows update from the expected patch directory. (T164-00280; T164-00286)

Immediately before that PowerShell execution, WS-JFROST-01 recorded a network logon by ali.hassan from WS-AHASSAN-01 and an associated privileged-logon event, consistent with the stated remote-patching practice. (T164-00268; T164-00269; T164-00270)

At 14:04:14 UTC, Explorer set a Julia-user UserAssist value whose ROT13-obfuscated name decodes to the Windows PowerShell executable path. This is a PowerShell-related user-activity marker, but it does not provide a command line or process parent. (T164-00343)

The documented, administrator-run patch command is evidence for benign PowerShell use at 13:45, but it does not establish what caused Julia's PowerShell-related UserAssist entry at 14:04 or whether that entry corresponds to the reported brief window. (T164-00280; T164-00343)

known_telemetry_limitations: The PowerShell-related UserAssist entry does not provide the executed command, process parent, or a directly linked process-creation event in the available records. (T164-00343)
The available records show the documented patch PowerShell execution at 13:45:45 UTC, rather than establishing a PowerShell process at the reported approximate time of 13:40 UTC. (T164-00280)
claims_not_established: The evidence does not establish whether Julia launched PowerShell at 14:04, what command or script may have run, or whether the UserAssist entry is connected to the ticketed report. (T164-00343)
The evidence does not establish malicious intent or activity in the documented ali.hassan patch execution. (T164-00280; T164-00286)
additional_evidence_needed: Collect PowerShell operational logs, including script-block and module logging if available, and EDR process-tree data for WS-JFROST-01 around 13:35–14:10 UTC.
Review UserAssist and other execution artifacts (such as Prefetch and Amcache) to determine whether Julia launched PowerShell and, if possible, when.
Ask Julia whether she saw or launched PowerShell and confirm with IT whether the 13:45 patch run explains the reported window.
unrelated_findings: WS-JFROST-01 authenticated to WS-NKIM-01 as noah.kim at 13:28 UTC; the destination recorded a network logon from WS-JFROST-01. This is separate from the PowerShell finding and merits review. (T164-00127; T164-00128; T164-00130)

Julia's Firefox session accessed Google Drive, including the shared-with-me page, despite Google Drive not being among the listed approved services. The records show browsing activity, not a confirmed upload or data transfer. (T164-00442; T164-00443; T164-00470)

Julia's Firefox session accessed Dropbox, which is not listed as an approved service. The records show page and resource requests, not a confirmed upload or data transfer. (T164-00626; T164-00627; T164-00635)

Cisco AnyConnect's VPN agent started on WS-JFROST-01, although the environment states there is no VPN and no approved remote-access service. The record does not establish that a VPN connection was made. (T164-00298; T164-00299)
